newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's prosecutor vows to defend journalists.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's prosecutor vows to defend journalists.

text.p: Ukraine's chief prosecutor vowed on Tuesday to defend journalists in the former Soviet republic after a leading newspaper editor was gunned down on his way to work.

Oleh Lytvak, acting prosecutor general who faces a daunting task uncovering crimes in the cash-starved country of 51 million, told a news conference his office would help journalists if they came under pressure.
"The prosecutor's office will be open to communication with representatives of the mass media," Lytvak told a packed hall.
"It is important to raise the issue of protecting journalists. There is a draft law being worked on and we expect it to be adopted," he said.

Borys Derevyanko, editor-in-chief of the Vechernaya Odessa daily in the Black Sea port of Odessa, was shot dead on his way to work on Monday morning in what the regional prosecutor said was an apparent contract killing.
He was the third reporter either to be killed or to die in suspicious circumstances in Ukraine this year.
Three scenarios were being considered -- that he was shot for his journalistic activities, for his work as a regional deputy or because of a personal vendetta, Lytvak said.
President Leonid Kuchma has launched a campaign to back journalists, who complain of coming under pressure or even fearing for their lives, especially if their beat covers crime.
One reporter covering a conflict between the mayor's office and security services in the eastern city of Lugansk was found dead in suspicious circumstances in his Kiev apartment in March.
Another was viciously attacked outside the capital in June and later died of his injuries in hospital.
